name: schema qualification stops being stripped, so `public.video_artifacts` matches no manifest name and an ordinary READABLE relation derives as OUT OF REACH (r9 M1)
expect: derive: a SCHEMA-QUALIFIED grant resolves to the bare manifest name

name: unquoted identifiers stop folding to lower case, so an UPPERCASE spelling of a granted relation no longer matches the manifest
edits: return name.lower()                  # unquoted: Postgres folds to lower case, so we must too
return name                          # unquoted: Postgres folds to lower case, so we must too
expect: derive: an UPPERCASE relation folds to lower case

name: quotes stop being stripped, so a quoted identifier keeps its quotes and matches nothing in the manifest
edits: return name[1:-1]                # quoted: case is PRESERVED, that is what quoting means
return name                      # quoted: case is PRESERVED, that is what quoting means
expect: derive: a QUOTED identifier resolves to the bare name

name: the GRANTEE side stops using the same normaliser as the relation side, so `to "anon"` matches nothing — the instance-not-class half of r9 M3
expect: derive: a QUOTED GRANTEE is still a session role

name: a grant to service_role counts as a SESSION read, so a relation only the service role may see is treated as reachable by anon
expect: derive: a service_role-only grant does NOT count as a session read

name: the out-of-reach set INVERTS — the relations the spec grants session SELECT on become the ones no session role may touch
edits: return tuple(sorted(r for r in relations if r not in readable))
return tuple(sorted(r for r in relations if r in readable))
expect: derive: a relation the spec grants no session SELECT on is OUT OF REACH

name: 05_assert.sql rejoins the corpus, so 2,500 lines of deliberately HOSTILE SQL — the thing that ATTACKS the contract — is read as the contract
edits: files = sorted(f for f in SPEC_DIR.glob("*.sql") if not f.name.startswith("05_"))
files = sorted(f for f in SPEC_DIR.glob("*.sql"))
expect: read_spec EXCLUDES 05_assert.sql — the hostile corpus is not the contract

name: function names keep their signature, so a manifest entry never matches the live function and the allow-list check compares two disjoint vocabularies
expect: m4_functions DERIVES names from the manifest, stripping the signature

name: VIEWS drop out of the derived relation set, so every M4 view is unaudited by a check whose subject is what anon can read
expect: m4_relations DERIVES names from the manifest, tables and views alike

name: the `uid` justification stops being checked against the body, so a function allow-listed for calling auth.uid() keeps its exemption after auth.uid() is removed
expect: kind 'uid' FAILS when auth.uid() is edited out

name: the `trigger` justification stops checking the return type, so any function may claim to be a trigger
expect: kind 'trigger' passes only for a trigger return type

name: the `readonly` justification stops looking for write verbs, so a function that gained an INSERT keeps its read-only exemption
expect: kind 'readonly' FAILS when a write verb appears

name: an UNKNOWN justification kind becomes a valid one, so a typo in the allow-list reads as a reason rather than as nonsense
edits: return False                      # an unknown kind is never a justification
return True                       # an unknown kind is never a justification
expect: an UNKNOWN kind is never a justification
